method: Static PE/CLR reverse engineering; no specimen execution or endpoint contact. Atomscan and cleave facts captured for all three originals. Rizin traces native code; ILSpy decompiles analysis-only metadata repair and recovered CLR stages.
external_context: Both supplied Triage report URLs were inaccessible. Verdicts rely on specimen bytes. No deployment authorization or provenance was available.

evidence: 0x40adbb copies Chromium Login Data, queries SELECT * FROM logins through dynamically resolved SQLite methods, and passes password blobs to CryptUnprotectData at 0x40afab.

0x40a50c fetches Mozilla NSS and runtime DLLs, writes them under GetTempPathW, and calls LoadLibraryW; these dependencies support NSS credential decryption. Raw-IP URLs do not identify a ShellExecute or remote-injection payload.

0x407488 installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL (13); callback 0x4074c0/0x4074d5 formats keystrokes including UTF-16 [ENTER] CRLF, tracks foreground input, and hands output to recording helper 0x407966. Helper 0x407966 opens the log with FILE_APPEND_DATA at 0x407a79 and writes the formatted window/keystroke record through WriteFile.

0x405172 receives framed socket data; 0x405263 dispatches decoded requests through 0x404a77. Kill calls at 0x402929 and 0x40c211 consume remote task parameters, not a demonstrated browser termination loop.

0x40f628 locates Explorer and calls 0x40f6ed, which writes a code stub/path into the remote process, changes protection, and starts a remote thread at code-buffer + 0x10e. No link to HTTP response bytes was established.
warzone160 is used in both protocol encode/decode paths; vendor family signatures corroborate the independently traced RAT capabilities.
samples.limits: No claim of observed exfiltration, successful remote execution, or browser killing. Legitimate administration context was not supplied; covert keyboard recording, broad password decryption and remote tasking tip the verdict.

evidence: ZIP member QUOTE NOVA TRADE 99286.bat is a .NET PE, not batch source. CLR root has duplicate empty shadow heaps and pointer tables mislabeled as compressed metadata.
An analysis copy renames duplicate heap headers, changes #~ to #-, and clears sorted-table hints for ILSpy. Original sample bytes are unchanged.

Main creates BankForm; its initializer calls XRun(Resources.OPlus,64512), reads RGB in column order, AppDomain.Loads the resulting bytes, selects GetTypes()[1].GetMethods()[0], and uses VB LateBinding.LateCall to invoke it.
OPlus BMP at file offset 0x1a1fe is 147x147. RGB columns reconstruct a valid managed PE identifying itself as HWMonitor Pro; its target is Form1.Justy.
Confuser constant pool uses a 16-word xorshift-generated XOR feedback key (seed 2525376191) followed by LZMA. Decoded dispatch values are Invoke, resource WGpA, project PeatBank, and hex key 766B68.

Justy crops WGpA by 177 columns and 225 rows, copies BGRA pixels in column order, reads an embedded length, and XOR-decodes with a last-byte-derived value and the first three UTF-16BE key bytes. The 808961-byte result is another managed PE.

Second recovered assembly presents Noogen Validation Engine identity. GetTypes()[7].GetMethods()[17] resolves to xbnkuu9ddH, which decodes another payload and has a branch that loads its bytes as an assembly and invokes EntryPoint.
samples.limits: Operational execution was not tested, and the ultimate payload family is not established. Concealed executable resources, chained automatic invocation and changing cover applications establish deception beyond ordinary image processing.

evidence: Entry 0x402674 calls main 0x401cb0. Config dword at 0x404120 is 3, selecting Active Setup routine 0x401900, followed by self-delete helper 0x401390.
0x401900 creates an HKLM Active Setup component and writes stubpath as REG_EXPAND_SZ at 0x401a4b; it copies/patches its own image using fread/fwrite and launches the installed path.
The mode-1 branch drops resource DLL and calls 0x401260, deleting and replacing LanmanServer Parameters/ServiceDLL with a different DLL path.

0x401150 creates a target process and performs VirtualAllocEx/WriteProcessMemory/remote-thread DLL loading with resolved-export handoff. 0x401390 constructs a COMSPEC /c del command using its own short module path.

Embedded resource DLL is 39936 bytes with Storm DDoS DNS banners and STORM command-format strings. Its AddressOfEntryPoint RVA 0x741a contains zero bytes, imports are damaged/bound, and it has no executable section.
samples.limits: The collector filename does not establish Remcos or WannaCry. Loader/injector and persistence code are present, but successful embedded-DLL execution or active flooding is not established. Existing four hostile code-oriented traits are retained.

trait_changes.retirement_reason: These profiles inferred source-to-execution flow, injection target linkage or browser killing from unrelated APIs/strings. Underlying neutral capability traits and stronger verified objectives remain. The browser-UA derivative shared the same unsupported source-sink premise.
trait_changes.relocations: Browser-store/process-kill source and PE profiles move to micro-behaviors/process/terminate/kill at notable, retaining neutral store alternatives. Objective SQL alternatives are removed to avoid an illegal capability-to-objective dependency. The redundant scope-union wrapper is removed. JS-only credential-source aggregation drops these non-JS, non-acquisition profiles.
trait_changes.new_coverage: Import-bound x86 SetWindowsHookEx type 13; native keyboard-record format; login-table query; keyboard recorder with DPAPI and NSS browser decryption.
trait_changes.corrections: UTF-16 Enter+CRLF bytes identify a record format, not a CLR runtime; rename and search all sections, updating both explicit consumers. DLL-suffixed HTTP URL is notable syntax, not suspicious behavior.
trait_changes.reference_audit: Exact and parent-directory consumers searched. Retired profiles have no remaining YAML references. Existing keylogger umbrella consumers keep their mechanism/runtime gates. Source and PE browser-store profiles keep separate format gates.
